override.repo_standard: docs/agents/CREW_CONTEXT.md, Verification Discipline: 'A check that cannot fail is indistinguishable from one that passed... mutate the thing it guards and watch it go red, then restore. If you mutate, assert the mutation actually applied.'
override.reason: The length is the standard being met, not padding. All six legs must run the SAME control-vs-mutant harness on the identical fixture and share the one assertNotEqual that makes a no-op leg impossible -- the exact defect that BLOCKed g2. Splitting into six methods would duplicate that harness six times and let one copy drift out of the paired assertion. The table entries are data, not branching: cyclomatic complexity is low and each leg is one tuple.

smells.finding: ArchiveReachabilityRuntimeTests holds 6 tests plus setUpClass/tearDownClass/resolved_c2b/run_command over one cohesive subject (the archive.c2b check text). Comparable in size to the file's existing GuardRuntimeTests. Single responsibility is intact.

The one repeated shape -- writing a python stub plus its /bin/sh shim -- is already factored into a two-iteration loop over (gh, git). The command text is never duplicated: it is read once from the resolved template and every variant is a .replace() on it, which is the whole point of the F2 remedy. No copy of the check text exists anywhere in the test file.

resolved_c2b reaches into the resolver module and the resolved JSON, and run_command reaches into checklist_engine._run_check_command. Both are deliberate couplings to the artifacts under test, not envy of a collaborator's data: the point is to measure the verdict the ENGINE would record on the text the TEMPLATE ships.

The mutation table's entries are bare 5-tuples (label, mutated, prs, control_passes, mutant_passes) whose last two fields are unlabelled booleans, repeated six times. Reading leg 5 requires counting positions to see that 'False, True' means the control fails and the mutant wrongly passes. Transposing those two booleans would silently invert a leg's meaning and the suite would still be green for five of six legs. A small namedtuple (or dataclass) with named control_passes/mutant_passes fields would make that class of edit impossible to make by accident. NON-BLOCKING observation: the current legs are correct -- I re-derived all six independently and every one discriminates -- so this is future-edit safety, not a present defect.
The check under test is handled as a raw string throughout, and every mutation is a str.replace / re.sub on it rather than a structured edit to a parsed command object.

override.repo_standard: g3-implement-HANDOFF.md cold critic finding F2, and docs/agents/CREW_CONTEXT.md 'Assert against behaviour, never against text that describes it' -- the test must read the shipped command OUT of the template, never restate it.
override.reason: A command-object abstraction would require parsing and re-serialising the shipped text, and any round-trip through such a model is a place the tested string can stop being byte-identical to the one that ships. Keeping it an opaque string is what guarantees the thing measured is the thing shipped. I verified this empirically: five template-level mutations all drove the suite RED, which a parsed-and-rebuilt copy could not guarantee.

At ff43e883 this was FLAGGED: the gh stub modelled three branches nothing exercised (--state closed, --state merged, bare 'length'), and unused modelled branches are exactly where a stub answers instead of refusing -- the same family as the c7 blocker. Commit 84d1e998 deletes all three. One branch remains technically unexercised -- --jq is still optional, with an else-branch printing raw JSON -- but I measured that drift at the shell rather than assuming: stripping --jq makes the command exit 2 in all three fixtures ('integer expression expected'), so it fails closed and is not the same hazard as a branch that answers a consumable count. Not flagged.

override.reason: These comments are not covering for unclear code; they carry required evidence that has nowhere else to live.
